seo.title: About ConvergeFlow | Revenue Cycle Workflow Views
seo.description: Learn about ConvergeFlow and its verification, eligibility, billing and receivables views. Explore the workflow and discuss your practice requirements.

blocks.text: ConvergeFlow is a revenue-cycle product with views for appointment verification, eligibility, claims and receivables. See upcoming appointment details and verification status together, then explore the later billing and balance views.

sections.title: About ConvergeFlow and the work your team reviews

blocks.text: The product discussion starts with the tasks your staff needs to understand. An upcoming appointment provides context for insurance review. A verification status or eligibility flag points to a question that needs attention. Claims, balances and reports extend that review into the later stages of the cycle.

ConvergeFlow includes interfaces for those areas. The details that matter to your practice include what the information means, where it comes from and who takes the next action. Confirm those details during evaluation.

sections.title: From individual tasks to practice context

blocks.text: Practice selectors, calendar views and reporting give the product conversation a wider frame. A single office may focus on the next appointment; a group may need to discuss how review responsibilities work across locations. Start with your organizational needs and confirm what the available views can support.

The [services overview](/services/) follows the broader revenue cycle. It provides a way to organize questions about registration, coverage, charges, claims, payments and follow-up without treating the diagram as proof of automated execution at every stage.

sections.title: Evaluate with your requirements in view

blocks.text: Specific requirements make the discussion useful. Bring your practice type, systems, payer questions and the information your staff needs to inspect. Keep examples de-identified and confirm the scope before assuming a workflow, integration or specialty is supported.
For a closer look at the evaluation criteria, read [Why ConvergeFlow](/why-convergeflow/). It explains which product details to examine and how to connect them to the work you need to review.

items.q: Does ConvergeFlow cover every stage automatically?
a: Confirm the available capabilities for each stage during evaluation. The revenue-cycle structure explains how the work connects, while a screen or menu shows an interface. Neither establishes automatic execution, payer coverage, processing accuracy or a specific outcome for your practice without further confirmation and evidence.

items.q: Is the product only relevant to dental practices?
a: Dental and medical practices have separate evaluation paths on this site. The observed account was dental-focused, so medical-specific workflows and requirements need confirmation. Bring your specialty, payer and system questions to the discussion rather than treating the audience label as proof that every use case is supported.

sections.title: Contact ConvergeFlow with the context that matters

Include your practice type and the stage you need to review, such as appointment preparation, eligibility, claims or receivables. You can mention a PMS or EHR name without sharing account credentials.

For group practices, explain which roles need to review the work and whether multiple locations are involved. For a medical or specialty practice, describe the specific requirements you need to confirm.

sections.title: Keep sensitive information out of your inquiry

blocks.text: Use business contact details and general workflow descriptions. sections.title: Explore before you ask

items.q: Can I use the demo request for patient or clinical questions?

Frame your question around the workflow and the information your staff needs to review, without sharing information that identifies a patient or provides access to an account.

items.q: What should I send before discussing an integration?
a: Start with the system name and the general information flow you need to support. Do not share login credentials, API secrets or exported patient data. Ask which interfaces and transactions are available, then confirm the required access and responsibilities through an approved process before connecting systems.

hero.title: How ConvergeFlow works: what to review in a demo

blocks.text: Start with an appointment and its verification status. Inspect the eligibility flags, then look at the claims, receivables and reporting views relevant to your team. Use these five steps to prepare the discussion.

sections.title: How ConvergeFlow works: start with the handoffs

blocks.text: A useful evaluation follows the information your team needs at each handoff. Identify what starts the work, who reviews it and what the next person needs to see. This keeps the discussion connected to your practice rather than a list of screens.

List where appointments, insurance details and billing records are held. Bring the names of your PMS or EHR and any other systems involved. Ask which connections are available and what information would need to move between them.

Describe the coverage, benefits or authorization questions your team needs to resolve. Separate the information you need from the decisions your staff must make. Confirm the scope for your payers and procedures during evaluation.

Look at appointment context, verification status and eligibility flags together. Then review the claims, receivables and reporting views relevant to your priorities. Ask what a status means, where its information comes from and how an unresolved item is represented.

Assign a person or role to each unresolved question in your proposed process. Discuss how that person would find the context and identify the next action. Confirm any routing, notifications or escalation requirements instead of assuming they are included.

Define the workload, review period and baseline you would use to assess a change. Keep measures specific to the workflow you are evaluating. Product views and general workflow goals do not establish an improvement without a consistent comparison.

sections.title: Bring a scenario, without patient information

blocks.text: A de-identified example makes the evaluation easier to follow. Describe an upcoming appointment with an unresolved insurance question, a claim needing review or an outstanding balance. Leave out names, identifiers, documents and clinical details.

items.q: Will the demo confirm every integration?
a: Use the demo to identify the connections your practice needs and ask what is supported. A system name on a screen does not establish a working integration. Confirm transactions, fields, access requirements and responsibilities before making an implementation decision or changing any existing systems.

items.q: Is this an implementation schedule?
a: This page describes an evaluation path. Implementation scope, responsibilities and timing need agreement after your requirements and available capabilities have been reviewed. Do not treat the steps as a promise of automated execution, a specific go-live date or a commitment to replace your current process.

hero.title: ConvergeFlow pricing: discuss your practice requirements

blocks.text: This page does not list fixed prices or packages. Use the demo request to discuss your workflow and ask for the applicable scope, charges and terms.

sections.title: Prepare for a ConvergeFlow pricing discussion

blocks.text: A clear requirements summary makes commercial questions more specific. Describe the parts of the cycle you want to review, the systems involved and the people who need to use the information. Do not include patient records or identifiable billing documents.

head: Bring this context
Ask this question
rows: Workflow priorities
Which capabilities are included in the proposal?
Practice structure and locations
What organizational scope does the proposal cover?
PMS, EHR and other systems
Which connections are supported, and what work is required?
Review and reporting needs
What access and reporting are included?
Expected rollout responsibilities
Which setup, training or ongoing services are included or separate?

blocks.text: These are questions to resolve, not a published pricing formula. Confirm any proposed fees and conditions in the commercial agreement.

sections.title: Review the total proposal

blocks.text: Compare the included scope with the work your team expects to do. Ask about recurring charges, any setup or usage charges, optional services and the conditions that could change the cost. Keep the answers with the proposal so the comparison remains clear.
Also review the term, renewal, cancellation and support provisions. An estimate or calculator can help organize assumptions, but it cannot establish a contractual price or guarantee a return.

items.q: Where can I find a published price list?
a: This page does not list fixed prices or packages. Use the demo request to start a discussion about your requirements and the relevant commercial proposal. Ask which charges are included, which may be separate and what scope or conditions apply before making a purchasing decision.

items.q: Is a free assessment or a trial included?
a: Confirm any trial, assessment or promotional offer directly during the commercial discussion. No such offer is promised on this page. Review any eligibility conditions, duration and included work in writing, along with the terms for continuing or ending the arrangement after an offer.

hero.title: Evaluate DSO revenue cycle management across your group

blocks.text: ConvergeFlow includes a practice selector, appointment calendar and revenue-cycle views. Bring one local-to-central handoff to the demo and confirm the reporting, access and ownership your group needs.

sections.title: What does DSO revenue cycle management need to show?

blocks.text: Start with the distinction between practice-level work and group-level oversight. List the appointments, claims and balances local teams review, then identify the questions your central team needs answered. Bring that structure to the demo. A practice selector provides context, but it does not establish consolidated reporting, access separation or support for your group’s operating model.

sections.title: How should work move between local and central teams?

blocks.text: Define the next owner at each handoff before evaluating automation. Choose an unresolved eligibility question, a claim requiring review and an outstanding balance. Ask how the available product represents each item and what information the receiving team can inspect. Confirm whether assignment, escalation and shared work queues meet your requirements rather than assuming those capabilities.

sections.title: How can you evaluate reporting across practices?

blocks.text: Compare report scope before comparing totals. Ask which practice and date filters apply, whether records can be combined and how access affects what a reviewer sees. ConvergeFlow has report controls and an audit activity view; group-wide aggregation and permissions remain requirements to confirm. Request evidence for the reporting structure your organization needs.

sections.title: What should your group prepare before the demo?

blocks.text: Prepare a list of practice systems, locations and review roles. Describe where responsibility changes between offices and the central team. Include the outputs needed for practice meetings and group reviews. Use synthetic records to discuss the workflow, and keep any rollout sequence conditional on confirmed integrations, access controls and implementation requirements.

sections.title: Use RCM resources to frame the next question

blocks.text: Start with the stage that creates uncertainty for your team. The questions below help you describe a workflow without sending patient records or assuming a particular product feature will resolve it.

Identify which appointment and insurance details staff need to review. Separate eligibility questions from the benefits detail or authorization information that may need further attention. Note who owns an unresolved item and when your team would look at it again.

seo.title: Insurance Eligibility Verification | ConvergeFlow
seo.description: Review eligibility verification with appointment context, task status and risk flags. Bring payer and practice requirements to a ConvergeFlow product demo.

hero.title: Insurance eligibility verification with appointment context

blocks.text: Keep the upcoming appointment beside the insurance question your team needs to review. ConvergeFlow includes a verification queue and an eligibility view with risk flags. Use those views to inspect the work ahead, then confirm available responses, fields and data flows for your practice.

sections.title: What eligibility verification needs to establish

blocks.text: Begin with the question and the appointment it relates to. Your team needs to distinguish the information returned from details that remain unclear. A task marked complete is not a promise that a claim will be paid. Keep unresolved coverage or authorization questions with the person responsible for the next review.

sections.title: See the task and its context together

blocks.text: The observed verification queue includes appointment and insurance context, status, search and filters. The eligibility view displays upcoming appointments beside risk flags. These views give your team a way to discuss which records need attention without treating a flag as a validated prediction of a claim outcome.

sections.title: Review a difficult appointment in the demo

blocks.text: Ask to inspect an appointment with information that needs clarification. Identify what the queue shows, what the flag means and where a reviewer can find the underlying information. Confirm which payer responses and benefit fields are available; the presence of report or verification controls does not establish completed processing.

sections.title: Keep the next handoff explicit

blocks.text: Patient eligibility verification belongs beside the next operational question. If the team needs to investigate an authorization requirement, use the [prior authorization evaluation page](/services/prior-authorization/) to prepare. If the next step is billing, compare the information reviewed with the [claims submission workflow](/services/claims-submission/). Confirm any product connection between stages.

items.q: Does an eligibility flag confirm coverage?
a: No. A displayed flag is a prompt for review, not confirmation that coverage applies or that a claim will be paid. Ask how each flag is defined and which information supports it. Your team should handle unresolved questions through its established payer and practice process before relying on a result.

items.q: Which payer responses are available?
a: The available payer responses have not been established by the read-only product review. It confirmed queue and eligibility interfaces rather than live processing. Bring the payers, information fields and service situations relevant to your practice, and ask to see what the product returns and how incomplete responses are represented.

items.q: Does a PMS name confirm an integration?
a: No. A system name or connection field does not establish a working integration. Confirm the supported system and version, which information moves between systems, and what implementation requires. Review update behavior and ownership of corrections before planning to rely on the connection for your appointment workflow.

items.q: Can medical and dental teams use the same workflow?
a: That requires practice-specific confirmation. The observed account was dental-focused, and medical-specific support has not been validated. Medical teams should bring their specialty, payer requirements and systems to the discussion. Dental teams should also confirm their required information and data flows instead of assuming the demonstration covers every use case.

seo.title: Prior Authorization Workflow Review | ConvergeFlow
seo.description: Prepare prior authorization questions, responsibilities and handoffs. Confirm available ConvergeFlow support for your practice during a product demo.

hero.title: Prior authorization workflow: requirements and follow-up

blocks.text: Prepare a clear record of the authorization question, the information needed and who follows up. Prior authorization execution in ConvergeFlow has not been validated. Use this page to plan the workflow you need and confirm available support in a product demo.

sections.title: Start with the requirement you need to confirm

blocks.text: Define the planned service and the authorization question through your practice’s approved process. Record the source of the requirement and what still needs clarification. Do not infer an authorization decision from an eligibility task status; the questions need their own evidence and review responsibilities.

sections.title: Keep the request context and next owner together

blocks.text: A useful review record identifies the appointment or service, the information gathered, the question still open and the next owner. If supporting material is needed, establish where staff prepare and review it. Keep sensitive records in your approved internal systems rather than submitting them through the public marketing website.

sections.title: What should a prior authorization workflow demo show?

blocks.text: Ask whether the product supports your authorization use case at all, then ask to see any available request, status and follow-up behavior. Distinguish a screen that holds notes from a workflow that sends information or receives a payer response. Record what is demonstrated and any step that remains outside the product.

sections.title: Connect authorization questions to the wider cycle

blocks.text: The [eligibility workflow](/services/eligibility-verification/) provides a starting point for discussing insurance context. The [claims workflow](/services/claims-submission/) helps define what the next reviewer needs before billing. These links describe related tasks; they do not establish an automated handoff or authorization capability in ConvergeFlow.

items.q: Does ConvergeFlow submit prior authorization requests?
a: That capability has not been confirmed. The reviewed evidence does not validate prior authorization submission or payer response handling. Use the demo to establish whether your required workflow is supported, which actions are available and which steps your practice must perform through its existing channels before making an implementation decision.

items.q: What should we bring to the discussion?
a: Bring your practice type, the systems involved and a de-identified description of an authorization question. Explain who prepares information, who checks status and who decides the next action. Do not include patient records, insurance documents or clinical details in a public demo request. Discuss an appropriate channel if further information is needed.

items.q: Does eligibility review settle an authorization question?
a: Do not assume that it does. Review what the eligibility information actually establishes and keep any authorization requirement visible as a separate question. Follow your practice’s approved process to confirm the relevant requirements. A product label or task status alone does not establish that the required authorization work has been completed.

items.q: Will the product replace our current process?
a: That has not been established. Describe your current process and ask which parts, if any, the available product can support. Confirm staff responsibilities, data sources and exception handling before changing an operating procedure. This page does not promise replacement of your existing tools, payer channels or review responsibilities.

seo.title: Claims Submission Workflow Review | ConvergeFlow
seo.description: Explore claims submission views, review questions and billing handoffs. Confirm available actions and data requirements in a ConvergeFlow product demo.

hero.title: Claims submission: inspect the queue and the handoff

blocks.text: ConvergeFlow includes claims, submission-queue, ERA/EOB and patient statement views. Inspect the context your billing team needs, then confirm available submission actions, checks and payer connections in a demo.

sections.title: Keep the claim record separate from the appointment task

blocks.text: The claims submission workflow needs its own record and status context. A completed verification task does not establish that a claim was prepared, transmitted or accepted. Bring the information your billing staff need from the earlier review and identify which details they must check through their established process.

sections.title: Inspect the billing views that were observed

blocks.text: The reviewed billing interface includes claims, a submission queue, ERA/EOB areas and patient statements. Those areas establish the visible scope of the module. The account reviewed did not validate live claim processing, so ask to see the actions and responses relevant to your practice rather than relying on a screen label.

sections.title: Ask what happens when a claim cannot proceed

blocks.text: An evaluation should include unresolved work as well as a successful-looking record. Ask which checks occur, how issues are displayed, where staff correct the source and how they know an action succeeded. Confirm whether any claimed scrubbing capability exists and what it examines before treating it as part of your process.

sections.title: Pass the right context into follow-up

blocks.text: Define the distinction between a submission status, a payer response and an outstanding balance. Use [denial management questions](/services/denial-management/) to plan review after an adverse response, and [AR management and reporting](/services/ar-management/) to inspect balance context. Confirm the available relationship between modules before planning a connected workflow.

items.q: Can ConvergeFlow transmit claims today?
a: Transmission has not been validated in the read-only review. The product includes claims and submission-queue interfaces, but those views do not establish that a claim can be sent through a particular clearinghouse or payer. Ask to see the supported action, response and requirements for your practice before relying on it.

items.q: Does the product scrub claims before submission?
a: Scrubbing behavior has not been confirmed. If your team needs claim checks, ask which fields or rules are examined, what the product reports and how staff resolve a flagged item. Do not assume that a submission queue includes automated checks or that any check guarantees acceptance or payment.

items.q: What should we inspect beyond the queue?
a: Inspect the source information, available actions and evidence of the resulting status. Ask what happens when an action fails or a response is incomplete. Include the staff member who owns corrections so your evaluation covers the next review step, rather than stopping at the appearance of a submitted label.

items.q: Does verification guarantee a clean claim?
a: No. Verification and claim preparation answer different questions. Keep the information reviewed, unresolved requirements and billing decisions separate. Follow your practice’s approved checks for the claim in question. Neither an eligibility flag nor a verification task status establishes that every claim requirement has been satisfied or that payment will follow.

seo.title: Denial Management Workflow Review | ConvergeFlow
seo.description: Plan denial review around the response, source evidence and next owner. Confirm available ConvergeFlow support for your follow-up workflow in a demo.

hero.title: Denial management: review the response and next action

blocks.text: Keep the response, supporting record and next review step together when work needs investigation. Dedicated denial-management execution in ConvergeFlow has not been validated. Use a demo to determine whether the available billing views support your review requirements and what remains with your team.

sections.title: Describe the issue before choosing an action

blocks.text: Begin a denial management workflow with the information actually received, rather than an assumed cause. Preserve the relevant response and its source in your approved record. Identify which question the next reviewer must answer before deciding how your practice should proceed.

sections.title: Give unresolved work an owner

blocks.text: A review record is useful when it explains what is known, what has been checked and who follows up. Separate a source-data question from a billing decision or a system issue. Establish a next action and review trigger through your practice process instead of leaving the record under an unexplained pending label.

sections.title: Evaluate the billing context without assuming a denial tool

blocks.text: ConvergeFlow includes claims and receivables interfaces, but that does not establish a dedicated denial queue, appeal workflow or automated correction capability. Ask whether your review scenario is supported, then inspect the available context and actions. Record steps that need another system or a staff-led process.

sections.title: Carry the result into the next stage

blocks.text: The [claims submission page](/services/claims-submission/) helps distinguish the earlier billing handoff. The [AR and reporting page](/services/ar-management/) explains questions to ask about balances and scope. In the demo, confirm whether and how a reviewed issue affects related records; do not infer a connection from adjacent navigation items.

items.q: Does ConvergeFlow automatically appeal denials?
a: Automated appeals have not been confirmed. This page explains a review workflow and does not promise denial recovery, payer contact or appeal submission. Ask which actions are available for your use case, who performs each action and what evidence is provided before planning to use the product for follow-up.

items.q: Will a denial view explain every cause?
a: Do not assume that it will. A response or status must be read with its source and available detail. Ask what information is visible, which questions still require investigation and how your team can record the next action. Product evaluation should distinguish displayed information from a confirmed explanation of an issue.

items.q: What does a useful review scenario include?
a: Use a de-identified description of the response, the information your staff checked and the question still open. Identify the person responsible for the next decision. Ask to see the available product context and actions, including what happens when the information is insufficient to proceed. Keep patient documents off the marketing form.

items.q: Can the product promise recovery or fewer denials?
a: No such outcome is established by the evidence available for this draft. A visible workflow does not demonstrate a financial result or a reduction in denials. Confirm product capabilities separately from any performance claim, and request relevant supporting evidence before using a result in your purchasing decision.

seo.description: Review AR management and reporting views, aging context and audit fields. Confirm data sources, available exports and practice requirements in a demo.

hero.title: AR management and reporting with balance context

blocks.text: Review insurance AR, patient AR, aging and balance views in ConvergeFlow. Inspect the report controls and audit fields, then confirm data sources, available actions and output scope in a demo.

sections.title: Understand the balance before comparing totals

blocks.text: Begin AR management and reporting with a clear question about the record and its scope. Identify the practice, date range and balance category you need to examine. A total without that context does not explain which account needs review or what the next staff member should investigate.

sections.title: Inspect receivables and aging views

blocks.text: The reviewed receivables interface includes insurance AR and patient AR areas, aging and balance views. These screens provide concrete structures to inspect during evaluation. Processing was not validated in the reviewed account, so confirm how records are populated and updated before relying on the figures for operating decisions.

sections.title: Ask what each report contains

blocks.text: The reports interface includes export controls, while the audit view includes timestamp, user, action, resource, details and IP columns. Exports were not run. Ask to inspect output fields, filters and scope, and confirm which activity is recorded. The presence of controls does not establish export behavior, retention or access policy.

sections.title: Turn a review question into an evaluation checklist

blocks.text: Choose an account question, name the record your staff expect to see and ask which view can answer it. Trace the data source and available date scope. Compare the [claims workflow](/services/claims-submission/) and [denial review](/services/denial-management/) when context from earlier work matters. Establish responsibility for any unanswered item.

faq.title: Questions about AR management and reporting

items.q: Does AR visibility mean collection work is automated?
a: No. A balance or aging view does not establish automated collection activity. The reviewed evidence confirms interfaces rather than operational results. Ask which actions are available, who performs follow-up and how changes reach the account record. Confirm those responsibilities before planning your receivables process around the product.

items.q: Can we export the reports?
a: Export controls were observed, but export execution and output content were not tested. Ask to see the available format, fields, filters and resulting file for your reporting question. Confirm the scope and behavior you need before promising a reporting output to another team or changing an existing reporting process.

items.q: Does the audit view establish compliance?
a: No. An audit interface provides activity fields to inspect; it does not establish a certification, regulatory compliance or a complete record of every action. Discuss your organization’s evidence requirements separately and request relevant documentation. Do not infer access, retention or data-protection commitments from the presence of an audit table.

items.q: Can reports show every practice in a group?
a: The product includes practice context, but the reporting scope needed for a group must be confirmed. Bring the practice structure and questions your team needs to answer. Ask how filters relate, which records are included and what comparison is valid before treating a summary as a group-wide operating view.

seo.title: RCM Security Evaluation Questions | ConvergeFlow
seo.description: Prepare an RCM security evaluation covering access, credentials, activity records and data handling. Discuss your evidence requirements with ConvergeFlow.

hero.title: Prepare your RCM security evaluation with clear evidence requests

blocks.text: Before connecting systems, identify the information involved, who needs access and the evidence your reviewers require. Bring questions about credentials, activity records, retention and data handling to the ConvergeFlow discussion.

sections.title: Where should an RCM security evaluation begin?

blocks.text: Begin with the proposed information flow and the systems involved. Identify which records your workflow would use, where information would move and who would be responsible for each step. Ask the product team to describe the available implementation and provide the documentation your organization requires. Keep unanswered questions open until the responsible reviewer has assessed the evidence.

sections.title: What should you ask about access and credentials?

blocks.text: Ask how users receive access, how permissions are changed and how access is removed. If a workflow needs external-system credentials, request details about storage, handling, use and administrative access. Confirm the controls for your proposed setup instead of inferring them from interface labels. This draft does not establish a particular access model or credential-management implementation.

sections.title: What does an audit activity screen establish?

blocks.text: An audit activity screen establishes visible fields to inspect, not complete event coverage or a compliance determination. The observed ConvergeFlow audit view includes timestamp, user, action, resource, details and IP address columns. Ask which events are recorded, who can view or export them, how long records remain available and how your reviewers would obtain supporting evidence.

sections.title: What evidence should your team request next?

blocks.text: Request the documentation relevant to your data-handling, access, retention and incident-response requirements. Ask which agreements apply to the proposed relationship and who can answer follow-up questions. The appropriate review depends on your organization’s responsibilities and intended use. Use synthetic examples during early discussions and keep sensitive records out of the public demo request.

sections.title: Explore the wider workflow

blocks.text: Use the [services overview](/services/) to frame the full patient-to-payment discussion. Review the [technology evaluation](/technology/) and security questions alongside your operating requirements.

items.q: Does an audit trail establish a security certification?
a: No. An audit interface does not establish a certification, regulatory compliance or complete control coverage. ConvergeFlow’s observed audit fields provide a starting point for questions about activity visibility. Request the evidence your organization needs and have the responsible reviewers assess it before connecting systems or making an implementation decision.

blocks.text: Describe the work your team needs to review and the questions an implementation decision needs to answer.
